user.title: How is the FC660 connected?
user.description: One entry per panel. Panels on one RS-485 bus are added one at a time, each with its own Modbus address, and share the connection.

network.title: Network gateway
network.description: A Modbus TCP gateway such as mbusd, or a transparent serial server (RTU over TCP). Use a gateway when other devices share the bus and something else polls them: RS-485 allows one master.

data_description.name: The device name. Its slug starts every entity id: "FC660" gives climate.fc660 and sensor.fc660_humidity, "FC660 Bedroom" gives climate.fc660_bedroom.
data_description.slave: Set on the panel (holding register 256); factory default 1.

serial.title: RS-485 adapter
serial.description: Terminals A/B on the panel, 8N1. Prefer a /dev/serial/by-id path: it survives reboots and replugging. Nothing else may open this port.

data_description.name: The device name. Its slug starts every entity id: "FC660" gives climate.fc660 and sensor.fc660_humidity, "FC660 Bedroom" gives climate.fc660_bedroom.
data_description.slave: Set on the panel (holding register 256); factory default 1.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Same panel, different link. Entity ids and history are kept.

error.cannot_connect: No answer. Check the host and port or the serial port, the Modbus address, and the wiring on A/B.
error.not_an_fc660: Something answered, but not like an FC660 at this address: {reason}.
error.invalid_name: Use a name with at least one letter or digit.
error.name_in_use: Another FC660 already uses the entity id prefix {prefix}. Choose another name.

abort.already_configured: This panel is already set up.

init.title: FC660 options
init.description: The panel is polled at the shortest of the three read intervals, and each read is made on the cycle nearest its own, so the other two round to a multiple of it. After a change from Home Assistant the settings are read back at once.

data.control_interval: Read power, mode and setpoint every
data.sync_clock: Keep the panel clock in sync

data_description.control_interval: Power, working mode, comfort/away and the setpoint (registers 264-268): what people change on the panel. One short read; 2 s is fine on a shared bus.
data_description.state_interval: Temperature, humidity, TVOC, CO2, the outputs (Y1, Y2, W1, W2, fan, …) and the fault code (registers 0-14).
data_description.settings_interval: Every setting and the panel clock (registers 256-279). Power, mode and setpoint come with it, so this read replaces that one when both are due.
data_description.unavailable_after: How long reads may fail before the entities show as unavailable. Short stalls on a shared bus are normal.
data_description.sync_clock: Set the panel's clock to Home Assistant's time whenever it is more than 2 minutes off (at most once an hour), daylight saving included. The panel's weekly programme runs on this clock.

cannot_connect.message: Cannot reach the FC660 at address {slave} on {endpoint}.

write_failed.message: Could not write {key}: {error}. Nothing was changed on the panel, or the next poll will show it.

write_not_applied.message: The FC660 accepted {key} but holds {held}, not {wanted}.

clock_not_applied.message: The panel clock reads {clock} after the sync.
